links.scope: All four access values, crossed with mute, for inbound and directly injected source events and for transport/intelligence targets.

links.scope: A statically muted readable transport or intelligence binding still receives the event and contributes tasks and observations.

assertions.proves: READ_WRITE and READ_ONLY readers retain exactly their task and observation with mute enabled or disabled; WRITE_ONLY and NONE targets do not react.
A buffered muted agent response is stored BLOCKED source_muted and reaches no transport; the trigger still opened its turn.

missing: Streaming mute transitions, unread stream closure, output_muted and mute/unmute lifecycle semantics remain outside this link.

links.scope: Rules 1-3 and 5 for static bindings: source refusal, readable targets, retained target effects and self-skip. Visibility is all throughout these matrices.
links.review: Read against Python source and specialized tests at fb46cb7bf and the current RFC. The full source unit is broader than these static-binding scenarios; no whole-section conformance is inferred.

assertions.proves: Inbounds and direct injections from NONE/READ_ONLY never reach any target, including when muted; WRITE_ONLY writes unless muted; self-reading produces no effects.
Only readable targets react; their tasks and observations survive mute and read-only access.
The public inbound result reports source_read_only when both access and mute prevent writing.
